an5.71:0.3.eng: Freedom of Heart is the Fruit (1st)

an5.71:1.1.pli: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā cetovimuttiphalā ca honti cetovimuttiphalānisaṃsā ca, paññāvimuttiphalā ca honti paññāvimuttiphalānisaṃsā ca.
an5.71:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, these five things, when developed and cultivated, have freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom as their fruit and benefit.

an5.71:2.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asubhānupassī kāye viharati, āhāre paṭikūlasaññī, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññī, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī, maraṇasaññā kho panassa ajjhattaṃ sūpaṭṭhitā hoti.
an5.71:2.2.eng: A mendicant meditates observing the ugliness of the body, perceives the repulsiveness of food, perceives dissatisfaction with the whole world, observes the impermanence of all conditions, and has well established the perception of their own death.

an5.71:2.3.pli: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā cetovimuttiphalā ca honti cetovimuttiphalānisaṃsā ca, paññāvimuttiphalā ca honti paññāvimuttiphalānisaṃsā ca.
an5.71:2.3.eng: These five things, when developed and cultivated, have freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom as their fruit and benefit.

an5.71:2.4.pli: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cetovimutto ca hoti paññāvimutto ca hoti—
an5.71:2.4.eng: When a mendicant has freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom,

an5.71:2.5.pli: ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘bhikkhu ukkhittapaligho itipi, saṅkiṇṇaparikho itipi, abbūḷhesiko itipi, niraggaḷo itipi, ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaṃyutto itipi’.
an5.71:2.5.eng: such a mendicant is one who is called ‘one who has lifted the cross-bar’, ‘one who has filled in the moat’, ‘one who has pulled up the pillar’, ‘one who is unimpeded’, and also ‘a noble one with banner lowered and burden dropped, detached’.

an5.71:3.1.eng: And how has a mendicant lifted the cross-bar?

an5.71:3.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno avijjā pahīnā hoti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā.
an5.71:3.2.eng: It’s when a mendicant has given up ignorance, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.

an5.71:3.3.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ukkhittapaligho hoti.
an5.71:3.3.eng: That’s how a mendicant has lifted the cross-bar.

an5.71:4.1.eng: And how has a mendicant filled in the moat?

an5.71:4.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ponobhaviko jātisaṃsāro pahīno hoti ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo.
an5.71:4.2.eng: It’s when a mendicant has given up transmigrating through births in future lives, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.

an5.71:4.3.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅkiṇṇaparikho hoti.
an5.71:4.3.eng: That’s how a mendicant has filled in the moat.

an5.71:5.1.eng: And how has a mendicant pulled up the pillar?

an5.71:5.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno taṇhā pahīnā hoti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā.
an5.71:5.2.eng: It’s when a mendicant has given up craving, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.

an5.71:5.3.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abbūḷhesiko hoti.
an5.71:5.3.eng: That’s how a mendicant has pulled up the pillar.

an5.71:6.1.eng: And how is a mendicant unimpeded?

an5.71:6.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni pahīnāni honti ucchinnamūlāni tālāvatthukatāni anabhāvaṅkatāni āyatiṃ anuppādadhammāni.
an5.71:6.2.eng: It’s when a mendicant has given up the five lower fetters, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them, so they’re unable to arise in the future.

an5.71:6.3.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu niraggaḷo hoti.
an5.71:6.3.eng: That’s how a mendicant is unimpeded.

an5.71:7.1.pli: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaṃyutto hoti?
an5.71:7.1.eng: And how is a mendicant a noble one with with banner lowered and burden dropped, detached?

an5.71:7.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno asmimāno pahīno hoti ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo.
an5.71:7.2.eng: It’s when a mendicant has given up the conceit ‘I am’, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.

an5.71:7.3.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaṃyutto hotī”ti.
an5.71:7.3.eng: That’s how a mendicant is a noble one with banner lowered and burden dropped, detached.”

an5.72:0.3.eng: Freedom of Heart is the Fruit (2nd)

an5.72:1.1.pli: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā cetovimuttiphalā ca honti cetovimuttiphalānisaṃsā ca, paññāvimuttiphalā ca honti paññāvimuttiphalānisaṃsā ca.
an5.72:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, these five things, when developed and cultivated, have freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom as their fruit and benefit.

an5.72:1.3.pli: Aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā—
an5.72:1.3.eng: The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of giving up, and the perception of fading away.

an5.72:1.4.pli: ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā cetovimuttiphalā ca honti cetovimuttiphalānisaṃsā ca, paññāvimuttiphalā ca honti paññāvimuttiphalānisaṃsā ca.
an5.72:1.4.eng: These five things, when developed and cultivated, have freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom as their fruit and benefit.

an5.72:1.5.pli: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cetovimutto ca hoti paññāvimutto ca—
an5.72:1.5.eng: When a mendicant has freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom,

an5.72:1.6.pli: ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘bhikkhu ukkhittapaligho itipi, saṅkiṇṇaparikho itipi, abbūḷhesiko itipi, niraggaḷo itipi, ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaṃyutto itipi’”.
an5.72:1.6.eng: such a mendicant is one who is called ‘one who has lifted the cross-bar’, ‘one who has filled in the moat’, ‘one who has pulled up the pillar’, ‘one who is unimpeded’, and also ‘a noble one with banner lowered and burden dropped, detached’. …”

an5.72:2.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno avijjā pahīnā hoti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā.

an5.72:2.3.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ukkhittapaligho hoti.

an5.72:3.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ponobhaviko jātisaṃsāro pahīno hoti ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo.

an5.72:3.3.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅkiṇṇaparikho hoti.

an5.72:4.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno taṇhā pahīnā hoti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā.

an5.72:4.3.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abbūḷhesiko hoti.

an5.72:5.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni pahīnāni honti ucchinnamūlāni tālāvatthukatāni anabhāvaṅkatāni āyatiṃ anuppādadhammāni.

an5.72:5.3.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu niraggaḷo hoti.

an5.72:6.1.pli: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaṃyutto hoti?

an5.72:6.2.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno asmimāno pahīno hoti ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo.

an5.72:6.3.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyo pannaddhajo pannabhāro visaṃyutto hotī”ti.

an5.73:0.3.eng: One Who Lives by the Teaching (1st)

an5.73:1.1.pli: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca:
an5.73:1.1.eng: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

an5.73:1.2.eng: “Sir, they speak of ‘one who lives by the teaching’.

an5.73:1.3.pli: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, bhikkhu dhammavihārī hotī”ti?
an5.73:1.3.eng: How is a mendicant who lives by the teaching defined?”

an5.73:2.1.eng: “Mendicant, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

an5.73:2.2.pli: suttaṃ, geyyaṃ, veyyākaraṇaṃ, gāthaṃ, udānaṃ, itivuttakaṃ, jātakaṃ, abbhutadhammaṃ, vedallaṃ.
an5.73:2.2.eng: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

an5.73:2.3.pli: So tāya dhammapariyattiyā divasaṃ atināmeti, riñcati paṭisallānaṃ, nānuyuñjati ajjhattaṃ cetosamathaṃ.
an5.73:2.3.eng: They spend too much time studying that teaching. They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.73:2.4.pli: Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu pariyattibahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
an5.73:2.4.eng: That mendicant is called one who studies a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.73:3.1.pli: Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhu, bhikkhu yathāsutaṃ yathāpariyattaṃ dhammaṃ vitthārena paresaṃ deseti.
an5.73:3.1.eng: Furthermore, a mendicant teaches Dhamma in detail to others as they learned and memorized it.

an5.73:3.2.pli: So tāya dhammapaññattiyā divasaṃ atināmeti, riñcati paṭisallānaṃ, nānuyuñjati ajjhattaṃ cetosamathaṃ.
an5.73:3.2.eng: They spend too much time advocating that teaching. They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.73:3.3.pli: Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu paññattibahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
an5.73:3.3.eng: That mendicant is called one who advocates a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.73:4.1.pli: Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhu, bhikkhu yathāsutaṃ yathāpariyattaṃ dhammaṃ vitthārena sajjhāyaṃ karoti.
an5.73:4.1.eng: Furthermore, a mendicant rehearses the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it.

an5.73:4.2.pli: So tena sajjhāyena divasaṃ atināmeti, riñcati paṭisallānaṃ, nānuyuñjati ajjhattaṃ cetosamathaṃ.
an5.73:4.2.eng: They spend too much time reciting that teaching. They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.73:4.3.pli: Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu sajjhāyabahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
an5.73:4.3.eng: That mendicant is called one who rehearses a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.73:5.1.pli: Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhu, bhikkhu yathāsutaṃ yathāpariyattaṃ dhammaṃ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati.
an5.73:5.1.eng: Furthermore, a mendicant thinks about and considers the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it.

an5.73:5.2.pli: So tehi dhammavitakkehi divasaṃ atināmeti, riñcati paṭisallānaṃ, nānuyuñjati ajjhattaṃ cetosamathaṃ.
an5.73:5.2.eng: They spend too much time thinking about that teaching. They neglect retreat, and are not committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.73:5.3.pli: Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu vitakkabahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
an5.73:5.3.eng: That mendicant is called one who thinks a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.73:6.1.eng: Take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

an5.73:6.2.pli: suttaṃ, geyyaṃ, veyyākaraṇaṃ, gāthaṃ, udānaṃ, itivuttakaṃ, jātakaṃ, abbhutadhammaṃ, vedallaṃ.
an5.73:6.2.eng: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

an5.73:6.3.pli: So tāya dhammapariyattiyā na divasaṃ atināmeti, nāpi riñcati paṭisallānaṃ, anuyuñjati ajjhattaṃ cetosamathaṃ.
an5.73:6.3.eng: They don’t spend too much time studying that teaching. They don’t neglect retreat, and they’re committed to internal serenity of heart.

an5.73:6.4.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, bhikkhu dhammavihārī hoti.
an5.73:6.4.eng: That’s how a mendicant is one who lives by the teaching.

an5.73:7.1.pli: Iti kho, bhikkhu, desito mayā pariyattibahulo, desito paññattibahulo, desito sajjhāyabahulo, desito vitakkabahulo, desito dhammavihārī.
an5.73:7.1.eng: So, mendicant, I’ve taught you the one who studies a lot, the one who advocates a lot, the one who rehearses a lot, the one who thinks a lot, and the one who lives by the teaching.

an5.73:7.2.pli: Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, satthārā karaṇīyaṃ sāvakānaṃ hitesinā anukampakena anukampaṃ upādāya, kataṃ vo taṃ mayā.
an5.73:7.2.eng: Out of sympathy, I’ve done what a teacher should do who wants what’s best for their disciples.

an5.73:7.3.pli: Etāni, bhikkhu, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni. Jhāyatha, bhikkhu, mā pamādattha, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha. Ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī”ti.
an5.73:7.3.eng: Here are these roots of trees, and here are these empty huts. Practice absorption, mendicant! Don’t be negligent! Don’t regret it later! This is my instruction to you.”

an5.74:0.3.eng: One Who Lives by the Teaching (2nd)

an5.74:1.1.pli: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca:
an5.74:1.1.eng: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

an5.74:1.2.eng: “Sir, they speak of ‘one who lives by the teaching’.

an5.74:1.3.pli: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, bhikkhu dhammavihārī hotī”ti?
an5.74:1.3.eng: How is a mendicant who lives by the teaching defined?”

an5.74:2.1.eng: “Mendicant, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

an5.74:2.2.pli: suttaṃ, geyyaṃ, veyyākaraṇaṃ, gāthaṃ, udānaṃ, itivuttakaṃ, jātakaṃ, abbhutadhammaṃ, vedallaṃ;
an5.74:2.2.eng: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

an5.74:2.3.eng: But they don’t understand the higher meaning.

an5.74:2.4.pli: Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu pariyattibahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
an5.74:2.4.eng: That mendicant is called one who studies a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.74:3.1.eng: Furthermore, a mendicant teaches Dhamma in detail to others as they learned and memorized it. But they don’t understand the higher meaning.

an5.74:3.2.pli: Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu paññattibahulo, no dhammavihārī’.

an5.74:4.1.eng: Furthermore, a mendicant rehearses the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it. But they don’t understand the higher meaning.

an5.74:4.2.pli: Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu sajjhāyabahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
an5.74:4.2.eng: That mendicant is called one who rehearses a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.74:5.1.pli: Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhu, bhikkhu yathāsutaṃ yathāpariyattaṃ dhammaṃ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati, uttari cassa paññāya atthaṃ nappajānāti.
an5.74:5.1.eng: Furthermore, a mendicant thinks about and considers the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it. But they don’t understand the higher meaning.

an5.74:5.2.pli: Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu: ‘bhikkhu vitakkabahulo, no dhammavihārī’.
an5.74:5.2.eng: That mendicant is called one who thinks a lot, not one who lives by the teaching.

an5.74:6.1.eng: Take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

an5.74:6.2.pli: suttaṃ, geyyaṃ, veyyākaraṇaṃ, gāthaṃ, udānaṃ, itivuttakaṃ, jātakaṃ, abbhutadhammaṃ, vedallaṃ;
an5.74:6.2.eng: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

an5.74:6.3.eng: And they do understand the higher meaning.

an5.74:6.4.pli: Evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, bhikkhu dhammavihārī hoti.
an5.74:6.4.eng: That’s how a mendicant is one who lives by the teaching.

an5.74:7.1.pli: Iti kho, bhikkhu, desito mayā pariyattibahulo, desito paññattibahulo, desito sajjhāyabahulo, desito vitakkabahulo, desito dhammavihārī.

an5.74:7.2.pli: Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, satthārā karaṇīyaṃ sāvakānaṃ hitesinā anukampakena anukampaṃ upādāya, kataṃ vo taṃ mayā.
an5.74:7.2.eng: Out of sympathy, I’ve done what a teacher should do who wants what’s best for their disciples.

an5.74:7.3.pli: Etāni, bhikkhu, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni. Jhāyatha bhikkhu, mā pamādattha, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha. Ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī”ti.
an5.74:7.3.eng: Here are these roots of trees, and here are these empty huts. Practice absorption, mendicant! Don’t be negligent! Don’t regret it later! This is my instruction to you.”

an5.75:1.1.eng: “Mendicants, these five warriors are found in the world.

an5.75:1.3.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco yodhājīvo rajaggaññeva disvā saṃsīdati visīdati na santhambhati na sakkoti saṅgāmaṃ otarituṃ.
an5.75:1.3.eng: Firstly, one warrior falters and founders at the mere sight of a cloud of dust. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

an5.75:1.5.pli: Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo yodhājīvo santo saṃvijjamāno lokasmiṃ.
an5.75:1.5.eng: This is the first warrior found in the world.

an5.75:2.1.pli: Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṃ;
an5.75:2.1.eng: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust,

an5.75:2.2.pli: api ca kho dhajaggaññeva disvā saṃsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṃ otarituṃ.
an5.75:2.2.eng: but he falters and founders at the mere sight of a banner’s crest. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

an5.75:2.4.pli: Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, dutiyo yodhājīvo santo saṃvijjamāno lokasmiṃ.
an5.75:2.4.eng: This is the second warrior found in the world.

an5.75:3.1.pli: Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṃ sahati dhajaggaṃ;
an5.75:3.1.eng: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest,

an5.75:3.2.pli: api ca kho ussāraṇaññeva sutvā saṃsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṃ otarituṃ.
an5.75:3.2.eng: but he falters and founders at the mere sound of turmoil. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to plunge into battle.

an5.75:3.4.pli: Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, tatiyo yodhājīvo santo saṃvijjamāno lokasmiṃ.
an5.75:3.4.eng: This is the third warrior found in the world.

an5.75:4.1.pli: Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṃ, sahati dhajaggaṃ, sahati ussāraṇaṃ;
an5.75:4.1.eng: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil,

an5.75:4.2.pli: api ca kho sampahāre haññati byāpajjati.
an5.75:4.2.eng: but he’s killed or injured when blows are struck.

an5.75:4.4.pli: Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, catuttho yodhājīvo santo saṃvijjamāno lokasmiṃ.
an5.75:4.4.eng: This is the fourth warrior found in the world.

an5.75:5.1.pli: Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, idhekacco yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṃ, sahati dhajaggaṃ, sahati ussāraṇaṃ, sahati sampahāraṃ.
an5.75:5.1.eng: Furthermore, one warrior can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil and being struck.

an5.75:5.2.pli: So taṃ saṅgāmaṃ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmo tameva saṅgāmasīsaṃ ajjhāvasati.
an5.75:5.2.eng: He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.

an5.75:5.4.pli: Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcamo yodhājīvo santo saṃvijjamāno lokasmiṃ.
an5.75:5.4.eng: This is the fifth warrior found in the world.

an5.75:5.5.pli: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca yodhājīvā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ.
an5.75:5.5.eng: These are the five warriors found in the world.

an5.75:6.1.pli: Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcime yodhājīvūpamā puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā bhikkhūsu.
an5.75:6.1.eng: In the same way, these five individuals similar to warriors are found among the monks.

an5.75:6.3.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu rajaggaññeva disvā saṃsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṃ sandhāretuṃ.
an5.75:6.3.eng: Firstly, one monk falters and founders at the mere sight of a cloud of dust. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.75:6.4.eng: Declaring his inability to continue training, he disavows it and returns to a lesser life.

an5.75:6.7.pli: ‘amukasmiṃ nāma gāme vā nigame vā itthī vā kumārī vā abhirūpā dassanīyā pāsādikā paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgatā’ti.
an5.75:6.7.eng: ‘In such and such a village or town there’s a women or a girl who is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.’

an5.75:6.8.pli: So taṃ sutvā saṃsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṃ sandhāretuṃ.
an5.75:6.8.eng: Hearing this, he falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.75:6.9.eng: Declaring his inability to continue training, he disavows it and returns to a lesser life.

an5.75:7.1.pli: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo rajaggaññeva disvā saṃsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṃ otarituṃ;
an5.75:7.1.eng: I say that this individual is like the warrior who falters and founders at the mere sight of a cloud of dust.

an5.75:7.4.pli: Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṃvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
an5.75:7.4.eng: This is the first individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.75:8.1.pli: Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sahati rajaggaṃ;
an5.75:8.1.eng: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust,

an5.75:8.2.pli: api ca kho dhajaggaññeva disvā saṃsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṃ sandhāretuṃ.
an5.75:8.2.eng: but at the mere sight of a banner’s crest he falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.75:8.3.eng: Declaring his inability to continue training, he disavows it and returns to a lesser life.

an5.75:8.5.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na heva kho suṇāti:
an5.75:8.5.eng: It’s when a monk doesn’t hear:

an5.75:8.6.pli: ‘amukasmiṃ nāma gāme vā nigame vā itthī vā kumārī vā abhirūpā dassanīyā pāsādikā paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgatā’ti;
an5.75:8.6.eng: ‘In such and such a village or town there’s a women or a girl who is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.’

an5.75:8.7.pli: api ca kho sāmaṃ passati itthiṃ vā kumāriṃ vā abhirūpaṃ dassanīyaṃ pāsādikaṃ paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgataṃ.
an5.75:8.7.eng: But he sees for himself a women or a girl who is attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty.

an5.75:8.8.pli: So taṃ disvā saṃsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṃ sandhāretuṃ.
an5.75:8.8.eng: Seeing her, he falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.75:8.9.eng: Declaring his inability to continue training, he disavows it and returns to a lesser life.

an5.75:9.1.pli: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṃ;
an5.75:9.1.eng: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust,

an5.75:9.2.pli: api ca kho dhajaggaññeva disvā saṃsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṃ otarituṃ;
an5.75:9.2.eng: but he falters and founders at the mere sight of a banner’s crest.

an5.75:9.5.pli: Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, dutiyo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṃvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
an5.75:9.5.eng: This is the second individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.75:10.1.pli: Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sahati rajaggaṃ, sahati dhajaggaṃ;
an5.75:10.1.eng: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest,

an5.75:10.2.pli: api ca kho ussāraṇaññeva sutvā saṃsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṃ sandhāretuṃ.
an5.75:10.2.eng: but he falters and founders at the mere sound of turmoil. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.75:10.3.eng: Declaring his inability to continue training, he disavows it and returns to a lesser life.

an5.75:10.5.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ araññagataṃ vā rukkhamūlagataṃ vā suññāgāragataṃ vā mātugāmo upasaṅkamitvā ūhasati ullapati ujjagghati uppaṇḍeti.
an5.75:10.5.eng: It’s when a mendicant who has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut is approached by a lady. She smiles, chats, laughs, and teases him.

an5.75:10.6.pli: So mātugāmena ūhasiyamāno ullapiyamāno ujjagghiyamāno uppaṇḍiyamāno saṃsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti brahmacariyaṃ sandhāretuṃ.
an5.75:10.6.eng: He falters and founders. He doesn’t stay firm, and fails to keep up the spiritual life.

an5.75:10.7.eng: Declaring his inability to continue training, he disavows it and returns to a lesser life.

an5.75:11.1.pli: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṃ, sahati dhajaggaṃ;
an5.75:11.1.eng: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest,

an5.75:11.2.pli: api ca kho ussāraṇaññeva sutvā saṃsīdati visīdati, na santhambhati, na sakkoti saṅgāmaṃ otarituṃ;
an5.75:11.2.eng: but he falters and founders at the mere sound of turmoil.

an5.75:11.5.pli: Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, tatiyo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṃvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
an5.75:11.5.eng: This is the third individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.75:12.1.pli: Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sahati rajaggaṃ, sahati dhajaggaṃ, sahati ussāraṇaṃ;
an5.75:12.1.eng: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil,

an5.75:12.2.pli: api ca kho sampahāre haññati byāpajjati.
an5.75:12.2.eng: but he’s killed or injured when blows are struck.

an5.75:12.4.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ araññagataṃ vā rukkhamūlagataṃ vā suññāgāragataṃ vā mātugāmo upasaṅkamitvā abhinisīdati abhinipajjati ajjhottharati.
an5.75:12.4.eng: It’s when a mendicant who has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut is approached by a lady. She sits right by him, lies down, or embraces him.

an5.75:12.5.pli: So mātugāmena abhinisīdiyamāno abhinipajjiyamāno ajjhotthariyamāno sikkhaṃ apaccakkhāya dubbalyaṃ anāvikatvā methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevati.
an5.75:12.5.eng: Without resigning the training and declaring his inability to continue, he indulges in sex.

an5.75:13.1.pli: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṃ, sahati dhajaggaṃ, sahati ussāraṇaṃ, api ca kho sampahāre haññati byāpajjati;
an5.75:13.1.eng: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil, but is killed or injured when blows are struck.

an5.75:13.4.pli: Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, catuttho yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṃvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
an5.75:13.4.eng: This is the fourth individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.75:14.1.pli: Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sahati rajaggaṃ, sahati dhajaggaṃ, sahati ussāraṇaṃ, sahati sampahāraṃ, so taṃ saṅgāmaṃ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmo tameva saṅgāmasīsaṃ ajjhāvasati.
an5.75:14.1.eng: Furthermore, one monk can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil, and being struck. He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.

an5.75:14.3.pli: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ araññagataṃ vā rukkhamūlagataṃ vā suññāgāragataṃ vā mātugāmo upasaṅkamitvā abhinisīdati abhinipajjati ajjhottharati.
an5.75:14.3.eng: It’s when a mendicant who has gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut is approached by a lady. She sits right by him, lies down, or embraces him.

an5.75:14.4.pli: So mātugāmena abhinisīdiyamāno abhinipajjiyamāno ajjhotthariyamāno viniveṭhetvā vinimocetvā yena kāmaṃ pakkamati.
an5.75:14.4.eng: But he disentangles and frees himself, and goes wherever he wants.

an5.75:14.5.pli: So vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ.
an5.75:14.5.eng: He frequents a secluded lodging—a wilderness, the root of a tree, a hill, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a forest, the open air, a heap of straw.

an5.75:15.1.pli: So araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā.
an5.75:15.1.eng: Gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, he sits down cross-legged, sets his body straight, and brings mindfulness to the present.

an5.75:15.2.pli: So abhijjhaṃ loke pahāya vigatābhijjhena cetasā viharati, abhijjhāya cittaṃ parisodheti;
an5.75:15.2.eng: Giving up covetousness for the world, he meditates with a heart rid of covetousness, cleansing the mind of covetousness.

an5.75:15.3.pli: byāpādapadosaṃ pahāya abyāpannacitto viharati, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī byāpādapadosā cittaṃ parisodheti;
an5.75:15.3.eng: Giving up ill will and malevolence, he meditates with a mind rid of ill will, full of sympathy for all living beings, cleansing the mind of ill will.

an5.75:15.4.pli: thinamiddhaṃ pahāya vigatathinamiddho viharati ālokasaññī sato sampajāno, thinamiddhā cittaṃ parisodheti;
an5.75:15.4.eng: Giving up dullness and drowsiness, he meditates with a mind rid of dullness and drowsiness, perceiving light, mindful and aware, cleansing the mind of dullness and drowsiness.

an5.75:15.5.pli: uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahāya anuddhato viharati ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto, uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṃ parisodheti;
an5.75:15.5.eng: Giving up restlessness and remorse, he meditates without restlessness, his mind peaceful inside, cleansing the mind of restlessness and remorse.

an5.75:15.6.pli: vicikicchaṃ pahāya tiṇṇavicikiccho viharati akathaṅkathī kusalesu dhammesu, vicikicchāya cittaṃ parisodheti.
an5.75:15.6.eng: Giving up doubt, he meditates having gone beyond doubt, not undecided about skillful qualities, cleansing the mind of doubt.

an5.75:15.7.pli: So ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe
an5.75:15.7.eng: He gives up these five hindrances, corruptions of the heart that weaken wisdom.

an5.75:15.8.eng: Then, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, he enters and remains in the first absorption …

an5.75:15.9.eng: second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.

an5.75:16.1.pli: So evaṃ samāhite citte parisuddhe pariyodāte anaṅgaṇe vigatūpakkilese mudubhūte kammaniye ṭhite āneñjappatte āsavānaṃ khayañāṇāya cittaṃ abhininnāmeti.
an5.75:16.1.eng: When his mind has become immersed in samādhi like this—purified, bright, flawless, rid of corruptions, pliable, workable, steady, and imperturbable—he extends it toward knowledge of the ending of defilements.

an5.75:16.2.pli: So ‘idaṃ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti,
an5.75:16.2.eng: He truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

an5.75:16.3.pli: ‘ime āsavā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ āsavanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti.
an5.75:16.3.eng: He truly understands: ‘These are defilements’ … ‘This is the origin of defilements’ … ‘This is the cessation of defilements’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of defilements’.

an5.75:16.4.pli: Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati,
an5.75:16.4.eng: Knowing and seeing like this, his mind is freed from the defilements of sensuality, desire to be reborn, and ignorance.

an5.75:16.5.eng: When it is freed, he knows it is freed.

an5.75:16.6.pli: ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.
an5.75:16.6.eng: He understands: ‘Rebirth is ended, the spiritual journey has been completed, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this place.’

an5.75:17.1.pli: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo sahati rajaggaṃ, sahati dhajaggaṃ, sahati ussāraṇaṃ, sahati sampahāraṃ, so taṃ saṅgāmaṃ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmo tameva saṅgāmasīsaṃ ajjhāvasati;
an5.75:17.1.eng: I say that this individual is like the warrior who can prevail over a cloud of dust and a banner’s crest and turmoil and being struck. He wins victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.

an5.75:17.4.pli: Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcamo yodhājīvūpamo puggalo santo saṃvijjamāno bhikkhūsu.
an5.75:17.4.eng: This is the fifth individual similar to a warrior found among the monks.

an5.75:17.5.pli: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca yodhājīvūpamā puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā bhikkhūsū”ti.
an5.75:17.5.eng: These five individuals similar to warriors are found among the monks.”
